title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: Remember, one-hot encoding is a way to represent categorical variables as binary vectors. For the $$job_{type}$$ variable, each category (blue collar, white collar, managerial) is represented by a separate binary column. In this case, since we're dealing with a white collar worker, think about which columns will be $$0$$ and which will be $$1$$.

title: Substitute Known Values
text: You know the worker is white collar and has $$10$$ years of education. Substitute these values into the equation: $$y=-8+3x_{edu}+6x_m-3x_b$$. What do you get when you plug in $$x_{edu}=10$$?

title: Calculate the Education Contribution
text: Calculate the contribution of education to the wage using the term $$3x_{edu}$$. What is the result when $$x_{edu}=10$$?

title: Consider the Job Type Contribution
text: Since the worker is white collar, the dummy variables for managerial $$x_m$$ and blue collar $$x_b$$ will both be $$0$$. How does this affect the equation?

title: Calculate the Predicted Wage
text: Now that you have the contributions from education and job type, calculate the predicted wage using the equation $$y=-8+3x_{edu}+6x_m-3x_b$$. What is the final result?
